title: Chaining Together Simple Modules to Create Complex Functions
summary: An early step toward constructive architectures that compose simple trainable modules into more complex functions.
growth_mechanism: Incremental composition of simpler learned modules into a larger function approximator.
notes: Seed bibliography item from the original project README. Needs full bibliographic verification.

title: Dynamic Node Creation in Backpropagation Networks
summary: Introduces Dynamic Node Creation, a constructive approach in which a backpropagation network can add hidden units during training instead of fixing hidden-layer size in advance.
growth_mechanism: Adds hidden nodes during backpropagation training when existing capacity appears insufficient.
notes: Seed bibliography item verified against Crossref for the Connection Science article. Semantic Scholar also indexes a 1989 IJCNN version with DOI 10.1109/IJCNN.1989.118509. Automated review draft still needs human full-text verification.

title: The Cascade-Correlation Learning Architecture
summary: Introduces a supervised constructive architecture that starts minimal, trains candidate units to correlate with residual error, installs the best unit, freezes it, and repeats.
growth_mechanism: Candidate hidden units compete by correlation with residual error; the best unit is installed and its incoming weights are frozen.
notes: Primary initial review target and anchor paper for early site demos.

title: Constructive Learning of Recurrent Neural Networks: Limitations of Recurrent Cascade Correlation and a Simple Solution
summary: Analyzes recurrent cascade-correlation, proves topology-driven representational limitations for some finite-state automata, and sketches a constructive fully recurrent alternative that adds neurons during training.
growth_mechanism: Constructively adds neurons during recurrent-network training while preserving a fully recurrent structure, proposed as an alternative to recurrent cascade-correlation's restrictive topology.
notes: Metadata verified against IEEE Xplore and Penn State Pure pages during the 2026-06-24 weekly discovery dry run. Keep title spelling as IEEE/PDF 'Cascade Correlation'; Penn State page title contains a likely 'Casade' typo.

title: Constructive Spiking Neural Networks for Simulations of Neuroplasticity
venue: PhD thesis, The University of Adelaide
summary: Develops a taxonomy for constructive neural networks and extends it into spiking simulations, proposing spike-timing-dependent construction and constructive algorithms for neuroplasticity-oriented simulations.
growth_mechanism: Treats growth as construction of neurons or synapses driven by constructive-algorithm processes; in the spiking branch these processes may depend on spike timing, local component performance, proxy-neuron events, or simulation expansion/contraction.
notes: Thesis source is public and maintained in a sibling repository. This web-book record points to a selective Chapter 2 taxonomy synthesis, not a verbatim thesis conversion.
